path_8 = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/test_8.csv"

# Read sources
Source9_18_0 = pd.read_csv(path_0, index_col=0)
Source9_18_1 = pd.read_csv(path_1, index_col=0)
Source9_18_2 = pd.read_csv(path_2, index_col=0)
Source9_18_3 = pd.read_csv(path_3, index_col=0)
Source9_18_4 = pd.read_csv(path_4, index_col=0)
Source9_18_5 = pd.read_csv(path_5, index_col=0)
Source9_18_6 = pd.read_csv(path_6, index_col=0)
Source9_18_7 = pd.read_csv(path_7, index_col=0)
Source9_18_8 = pd.read_csv(path_8, index_col=0)
Source9_18_9 = pd.read_csv(path_9, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source9_18_4 and Source9_18_0 on zipcode
# Source9_18_4: ['boro', 'zipcode']
# Source9_18_0: ['zipcode', 'total_crime', 'violation', 'misdemeanor', 'felony']
# Join on 'zipcode'
join_4_0 = pd.merge(Source9_18_4, Source9_18_0, on="zipcode", how="inner")

# Operation 2: JOIN Source9_18_1 and Source9_18_3 on ['zipcode', 'businesses']
# Source9_18_1: ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
# Source9_18_3: ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
join_1_3 = pd.merge(Source9_18_1, Source9_18_3, on=["zipcode", "businesses"], how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Operation 3: JOIN Source9_18_9 and Source9_18_7 on ['zipcode', 'businesses']
# Source9_18_9: ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
# Source9_18_7: ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
join_9_7 = pd.merge(Source9_18_9, Source9_18_7, on=["zipcode", "businesses"], how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Operation 4: JOIN Source9_18_6 and Source9_18_8 on 'zipcode'
# Source9_18_6: ['zipcode', 'counts']
# Source9_18_8: ['zipcode', 'counts']
join_6_8 = pd.merge(Source9_18_6, Source9_18_8, on="zipcode", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Operation 5: JOIN Source9_18_2 and Source9_18_4 on 'zipcode'
# Source9_18_2: ['zipcode', 'indicator', 'counts']
# Source9_18_4: ['boro', 'zipcode']
# We already have Source9_18_4 joined with Source9_18_0 in join_4_0, but operation says join Source9_18_2 and Source9_18_4
join_2_4 = pd.merge(Source9_18_2, Source9_18_4, on="zipcode", how="inner")

# Now, we need to combine all these joins into one dataframe keyed on zipcode.
# The target schema columns and the example show that the final table has columns from all these joins.

# To combine, we will join all intermediate results on 'zipcode' step by step.

# Start from join_4_0 (has boro, zipcode, total_crime, violation, misdemeanor, felony)
df = join_4_0.copy()

# Join join_1_3 on 'zipcode'
# join_1_3 has columns: zipcode, businesses_x, counts_x, businesses_y, counts_y
# We want to keep these columns with suffixes as is.
df = pd.merge(df, join_1_3, on="zipcode", how="left")

# Join join_9_7 on 'zipcode'
# join_9_7 has columns: zipcode, businesses_x, counts_x, businesses_y, counts_y
# To avoid column name collision, rename these columns before merging
join_9_7_renamed = join_9_7.rename(columns={
    "businesses_x": "businesses_x_5",
    "counts_x": "counts_x_6",
    "businesses_y": "businesses_y_7",
    "counts_y": "counts_y_8"
})
df = pd.merge(df, join_9_7_renamed, on="zipcode", how="left")

# Join join_6_8 on 'zipcode'
# join_6_8 has columns: zipcode, counts_x, counts_y
# Rename to counts_x_10 and counts_y_11 to match target schema
join_6_8_renamed = join_6_8.rename(columns={
    "counts_x": "counts_x_10",
    "counts_y": "counts_y_11"
})
df = pd.merge(df, join_6_8_renamed, on="zipcode", how="left")

# Join join_2_4 on 'zipcode'
# join_2_4 has columns: zipcode, indicator, counts, boro
# We already have boro from join_4_0, so to avoid conflict, drop boro from join_2_4 before merging
join_2_4_drop_boro = join_2_4.drop(columns=["boro"])
df = pd.merge(df, join_2_4_drop_boro, on="zipcode", how="left")

# Join Source9_18_5 (zipcode, theft, assault, harassment)
df = pd.merge(df, Source9_18_5, on="zipcode", how="left")

# Now, according to the group_by and aggregations operation:
# group_by = [Source9_18_0.zipcode]
# aggregations = sum of many columns from different sources:
# sum(Source9_18_0.total_crime), sum(Source9_18_0.violation), sum(Source9_18_0.misdemeanor), sum(Source9_18_0.felony),
# sum(Source9_18_1.counts), sum(Source9_18_3.counts), sum(Source9_18_9.counts), sum(Source9_18_7.counts),
# sum(Source9_18_2.counts), sum(Source9_18_5.theft), sum(Source9_18_5.assault), sum(Source9_18_5.harassment),
# sum(Source9_18_6.counts), sum(Source9_18_8.counts)

# But since we have already joined and have these counts in columns, we will group by zipcode and sum these columns.

# Columns to sum (mapped to current df columns):
# total_crime, violation, misdemeanor, felony (from Source9_18_0)
# counts_x (from join_1_3) -> counts_x
# counts_y (from join_1_3) -> counts_y
# counts_x_6 (from join_9_7) -> counts_x_6
# counts_y_8 (from join_9_7) -> counts_y_8
# counts (from join_2_4) -> counts (indicator counts)
# theft, assault, harassment (from Source9_18_5)
# counts_x_10 (from join_6_8) -> counts_x_10
# counts_y_11 (from join_6_8) -> counts_y_11

# Note: counts from Source9_18_3 and Source9_18_9 are included in counts_y and counts_x_6 respectively after joins.

# We also have businesses columns which are strings and should not be aggregated.

# For businesses columns, since they are strings and come from joins on zipcode and businesses, 
# we will take the first non-null value per zipcode (assuming one unique per zipcode in each join).

# Prepare aggregation dictionary:
agg_dict = {
    'total_crime': 'sum',
    'violation': 'sum',
    'misdemeanor': 'sum',
    'felony': 'sum',
    'counts_x': 'sum',
    'counts_y': 'sum',
    'counts_x_6': 'sum',
    'counts_y_8': 'sum',
    'counts': 'sum',  # from join_2_4 (indicator counts)
    'theft': 'sum',
    'assault': 'sum',
    'harassment': 'sum',
    'counts_x_10': 'sum',
    'counts_y_11': 'sum',
    # For businesses columns, take first non-null value
    'businesses_x': 'first',
    'businesses_y': 'first',
    'businesses_x_5': 'first',
    'businesses_y_7': 'first',
    'boro': 'first',
    'indicator': 'first'
}

# Some columns might have NaNs, fill them with appropriate defaults before aggregation
# For counts columns fillna(0), for strings fillna('')

# Fill NaNs for counts columns with 0
counts_columns = ['total_crime', 'violation', 'misdemeanor', 'felony',
                  'counts_x', 'counts_y', 'counts_x_6', 'counts_y_8',
                  'counts', 'theft', 'assault', 'harassment',
                  'counts_x_10', 'counts_y_11']
df[counts_columns] = df[counts_columns].fillna(0)

# Fill NaNs for string columns with empty string
string_columns = ['businesses_x', 'businesses_y', 'businesses_x_5', 'businesses_y_7', 'boro', 'indicator']
df[string_columns] = df[string_columns].fillna('')

# Group by zipcode and aggregate
df_grouped = df.groupby('zipcode', as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['zipcode': integer, 'businesses_x': string, 'counts_x': integer, 'businesses_y': string, 'counts_y': integer,
#  'businesses_x_5': string, 'counts_x_6': integer, 'businesses_y_7': string, 'counts_y_8': integer,
#  'boro': string, 'counts_x_10': integer, 'counts_y_11': integer, 'indicator': string, 'counts': integer,
#  'total_crime': integer, 'violation': integer, 'misdemeanor': integer, 'felony': integer,
#  'theft': integer, 'assault': integer, 'harassment': integer]

final_columns = [
    'zipcode',
    'businesses_x',
    'counts_x',
    'businesses_y',
    'counts_y',
    'businesses_x_5',
    'counts_x_6',
    'businesses_y_7',
    'counts_y_8',
    'boro',
    'counts_x_10',
    'counts_y_11',
    'indicator',
    'counts',
    'total_crime',
    'violation',
    'misdemeanor',
    'felony',
    'theft',
    'assault',
    'harassment'
]

# Ensure all columns exist in df_grouped, if not create with default values
for col in final_columns:
    if col not in df_grouped.columns:
        if col in counts_columns:
            df_grouped[col] = 0
        else:
            df_grouped[col] = ''

# Select and reorder columns
df_final = df_grouped[final_columns]

# Cast columns to correct types as per target schema
df_final = df_final.astype({
    'zipcode': 'int64',
    'businesses_x': 'string',
    'counts_x': 'int64',
    'businesses_y': 'string',
    'counts_y': 'int64',
    'businesses_x_5': 'string',
    'counts_x_6': 'int64',
    'businesses_y_7': 'string',
    'counts_y_8': 'int64',
    'boro': 'string',
    'counts_x_10': 'int64',
    'counts_y_11': 'int64',
    'indicator': 'string',
    'counts': 'int64',
    'total_crime': 'int64',
    'violation': 'int64',
    'misdemeanor': 'int64',
    'felony': 'int64',
    'theft': 'int64',
    'assault': 'int64',
    'harassment': 'int64'
})

# Write the final dataframe to CSV
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/target_multisource.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
